key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within seconds. LOCATION: UNILATERAL facial pain. DURATION: Lasts seconds to minutes. CHARACTER: SEVERE, SHARP, ELECTRIC-like pain. AGGRAVATING: TOUCH, speaking, eating, brushing teeth. RELIEVING: ANTICONVULSANTS, avoiding triggers. TIMING: Sudden onset, lasts seconds to minutes. SEVERITY: 8-10/10, severe and unrelenting. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: SEVERE FACIAL PAIN, may have facial twitching, may have difficulty speaking, eating. KEY POSITIVES: Severe facial pain, electric-like pain, trigger points. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Severe facial pain with other neurological deficits - possible stroke, call 911
Facial pain with signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Facial pain with severe hypertension - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Facial pain with signs of brainstem involvement - dysphagia, dysarthria, ataxia - call 911
Facial pain with signs of respiratory failure - difficulty breathing, cyanosis, altered mental status - call 911
